decisions: Handlers are named GetMaintenancePlanHandler, GetMaintenancePlanSummariesHandler, GetOdometerReadingsHandler, SearchAlertsHandler, GetRoutineTypesHandler; queries stay in their feature folder.
Infra query classes are public sealed and take MaintenanceDbContext; the host must register them as scoped for the IXxxQueries ports (no AddQueryHandlers scan covers them).
Plan summaries and details count only active routines; InactiveCount is separate. Pistas km/time come from the domain evaluators in the Infrastructure projector.

DI must register scoped IMaintenancePlanRepository, IRoutineTypeRepository, IAlertRepository, IOdometerReadingLog and IUnitOfWork->MaintenanceUnitOfWork (after AddRutaVivaPersistence), plus singleton …
GetActivePlanIdsPageAsync uses FromSqlRaw 'WHERE [VehicleId] > {0}' (Guid.Empty when after is null) so the keyset order matches SQL Server uniqueidentifier ordering.
GetCatalogAsync uses a tracked ToListAsync on RoutineTypes, so already-tracked entities with unsaved changes win over database values.
AddMaintenance reads ConnectionStrings:RutaViva eagerly and throws InvalidOperationException if missing; EventBus:HubUrl is read lazily from configuration.
Domain-event handlers and integration-event mappers are registered as Scoped via a Scrutor scan of the Application assembly; IUnitOfWorkScopeFactory is Singleton.
AddMaintenance registers TimeProvider.System and SystemClock through TryAdd, so a host can override them.
Strong IDs serialize as plain GUID strings via MaintenanceIdJsonConverterFactory, registered in Program.cs with ConfigureHttpJsonOptions; without it DTOs would emit {value:...}.
UpdatedBy/AcknowledgedBy come from the request body (no auth yet). PUT/PATCH commands answer 204 via ToNoContentResult; failures use ToHttpResult.
Request field is dueSoonThresholdPercent (spec name) for routine and routine-type PUT; no PATCH plan status route because the registry has none.
